question.text: An investor has the following capital gains in FY 2025-26: Short-term capital loss of Rs. 80,000 from equity MF, Long-term capital gain of Rs. 2,50,000 from equity MF, and Short-term capital gain of Rs. 40,000 from debt MF. Assuming the investor adopts the tax-minimising set-off order (setting off the short-term capital loss first against the short-term capital gain taxed at the higher rate, and then any remaining short-term capital loss against the long-term capital gain), what are the net taxable gains after set-off?

answer.text: LTCG of Rs. 2,50,000 and STCG of Rs. 40,000 (losses cannot be set off across types)
LTCG of Rs. 1,70,000 and STCG of Rs. 40,000 (STCL set off only against LTCG)
Net STCG = Nil (after setting off Rs. 40,000 STCL against STCG) and Net LTCG = Rs. 2,10,000 (after setting off remaining Rs. 40,000 STCL against LTCG)
Net STCG = Rs. 40,000 and Net LTCG = Rs. 1,70,000 (STCL set off only against LTCG first)

explanation.text: The Logic: The Income-tax Act permits STCL to be set off against both STCG and LTCG, but it does not prescribe an order. Under the tax-minimising order specified in the stem, the investor first sets off Rs. 40,000 of STCL against the Rs. 40,000 STCG taxed at the higher slab/special rate (Net STCG = Nil), and then sets off the remaining Rs. 40,000 of STCL against LTCG of Rs. 2,50,000 (Net LTCG = Rs. 2,10,000). This minimises the overall tax outflow because STCG on debt MF is taxed at slab rate, which is typically higher than the 12.5% LTCG rate on equity MF. The Trap: Option A wrongly claims losses cannot cross types - workbook p.160 expressly allows STCL to be set off against both STCG and LTCG. Option B incorrectly sets off all STCL only against LTCG. Option D reverses the optimal order. The audit flagged this item because the workbook only states the set-off rule, not the order; without an ordering instruction in the stem, both Option C and Option D were defensible. Note: The original stem did not specify the set-off order, which left multiple net-gain presentations supportable from NISM Series V-A (p.160). The stem has been tightened to specify the tax-minimising set-off order, making Option C the uniquely correct net-gain pair.
